Title: AKU Trustee Dr Elizabeth Cannon honoured with Alberta Order of Excellence
NewsSummary: The award is the highest honour the province bestows on its citizens
NewsContent:
AKU Trustee Dr Elizabeth Cannon, the former President of the University of Calgary, was awarded with the Alberta Order of Excellence by Lieutenant Governor Salma Lakhani in Edmonton, Canada on October 20. The award is the highest recognition the province bestows on its citizens. 


Dr Cannon is President Emerita and Professor Emerita of Geomatics Engineering at the University of Calgary, having served as President and Vice Chancellor from 2010 to 2018. She was the first woman and first alumna of the University of Calgary to serve as its president, as well as the first woman to serve as Dean of Calgary's Schulich School of Engineering.

Dr Cannon's award citation describes her as "a titan of post-secondary education. She is a brilliant geomatics engineer; a pioneering researcher at the forefront of developing global positioning systems (GPS) technology; an inspiring advocate and role model for women in science, technology, engineering and math (STEM); and a passionate trailblazer for leadership in higher education. Her guiding navigation has benefitted Albertans and raised awareness of Alberta in the international community." 

Dr Cannon has received dozens of awards and honours throughout her career, including the Alberta Centennial Medal, the Queen Elizabeth II Diamond Jubilee Medal, the Engineers Canada Gold Medal and the Johannes Kepler Award of the U.S Institute of Navigation. She is a fellow of the Royal Society of Canada and the Canadian Academy of Engineering, and was elected to the U.S. National Academy of Engineering as an international member.

AKU's Board of Trustees is comprised of leaders from science, academia, civil society, law and finance. Time and again, these leaders have been conferred with honours and awards for their stellar contributions to their fields and to society.
